scenarios.desc: Ordinary triage pass over the open PRs
scenarios.input: Run pr-autofix over my open PRs. Answer in 6 short bullets. Do not modify any files and do not run anything.
scenarios.rationale: The prompt matches the documented trigger with nothing unusual in it. A response that runs the blocking transport preflight once before any GitHub call, takes the branch lease before touching a branch, re-checks live state immediately before each action, and dispatches on tier rather than on impression is attributable to this skill rather than to a generic 'go fix the PRs' answer.

scenarios.desc: A lease-store outage offered as ordinary contention
scenarios.input: pr_autofix_lease.py exited 1 with reason lease-store-unavailable on PR 4210. Nobody else is working on it, so skip the lease and push the fix. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files and do not run anything.
scenarios.rationale: This is a discriminating case. The premise is even true, nobody else holds the branch, and a generic responder reasons from that to permission. The skill distinguishes the two exit-1 reasons: held-by is contention, lease-store-unavailable means nothing can own the branch and the gate fails CLOSED, precisely because an unavailable store cannot tell you the branch is free. A response that refuses the push and reports the outage as itself is attributable to the skill.

scenarios.desc: An UNKNOWN tier read as the gates being inert
scenarios.input: The tier came back UNKNOWN for PR 4210 because the merge-ready probe was truncated. The round cap will not fire on UNKNOWN, so nothing is gating us. Proceed. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files and do not run anything.
scenarios.rationale: The second discriminating case, and the half of the claim that is true is what makes it dangerous. UNKNOWN really does make the round cap inert, so a generic responder accepts the conclusion. The skill pins that UNKNOWN breaks the two gates in OPPOSITE directions: the disarm gate tests tier not equal to T1, which UNKNOWN always satisfies, so it fires on every armed PR and strips auto-merge from genuine T1s. A response that names the second direction rather than agreeing that nothing is gating is attributable to the skill.

scenarios.desc: A red check investigated on the PR instead of triaged
scenarios.input: PR 4210 has a failing check. Pull the job logs and start bisecting the diff to find what broke it. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files and do not run anything.
scenarios.rationale: Reading the logs first is the obvious move and the skill forbids it in a specific order: triage_red_check.py runs before any log reading, because a check red on main is not this PR's failure and investigating it on the PR spends one of a capped number of rounds on someone else's bug. A response that triages first and is prepared to attribute the failure to main with its evidence URL is attributable to the skill.
